## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Serīsakavimānavatthu* (Vv 84) is a canonical text in the *Vimānavatthu* collection of the Pali Khuddaka Nikāya [SuttaCentral]. In this narrative, a deity named Serīsaka recounts how he arrived at his comfortable existence in the heavenly realms and advises listeners on the righteous conduct necessary to achieve a similar rebirth [SuttaCentral]. Scholarly annotations note that in Pali traditions the *serīsakavimāna* designates a celestial palace situated in the realm of the Cāturmahārājika deities [Lamotte 1970]. In studies of doctrinal terminology, the text is cited alongside its *Petavatthu* twin for its use of the verbal form *adhitthahātha* ("resolutely determine") in the exhortation *dhammānuyogañca adhitthahātha* ("resolutely determine on the practice of the Dhamma") [Lim Hwee San 2009].
Curated parallels on SuttaCentral identify the text as fully parallel to the *Serīsakapetavatthu* (Pv 37), with cross-references occurring in the *Saṅkhapālajātaka* (Ja 524) and *Vidhurajātaka* (Ja 546) [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus strongly confirms these interrelations through automatic text-reuse analysis: segments §1.1–55.1 show a complete 1.0 similarity match with *Serīsakapetavatthu* (Pv 37), and verses §22.1–24.2 recur verbatim in both *Vidhurajātaka* (Ja 546) and *Saṅkhapālajātaka* (Ja 524), as well as in their respective *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* sections [DharmaNexus]. Text reuse is also extensive in the *Vimānavatthu-aṭṭhakathā* and *Petavatthu-aṭṭhakathā*, while formulaic lines in §50.3–50.6 are shared with other stories including *Maṭṭhakuṇḍalīvimānavatthu* (Vv 83) and *Maṭṭhakuṇḍalīpetavatthu* (Pv 17) [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also records lower-level cross-language alignments with Sanskrit and Tibetan philosophical and narrative texts (such as Śāntideva's *Bodhicaryāvatāra* and the *Lokaprajñapti*) and the Chinese *Madhyama Āgama* [DharmaNexus].
